displayName: Le Ptit italien finition de Beton
description:
Type de projet: Site web.

Qui est-ce pour ?: Petite compagnie miniature ("Le petit italien finition de plancher de béton").

But: Mettre en valeur l'expertise de finisseur de plancher de béton.

Fonctionnalités clés:
- Coordonnées de contact.
- Galerie photos/vidéos des travaux (ex: planchers avec flatteuses, fini terrazzo).
- Section possible pour témoignages clients (satisfaction garantie).

Design & marque:
- Intégrer le logo existant créé par son garçon.
- Le design est laissé à la discrétion du réalisateur (le client n'a pas de préférence de couleur).

Intégrations & extras:
- Slogan/Devise: "Quand j'ai terminé le plancher, vous marcherez sur mon plancher ou vous ne me payez pas".

Services supplémentaires:
- Pose d'acrylique sur les murs.
- Plâtrage.
- Réparation de solage extérieur.
- Acrylique de toutes les couleurs.

Contexte d'affaires:
- Forte saisonnalité: la demande commence avec l'été et s'intensifie avant les vacances de la construction et le retour du froid. Le client souhaite attirer plus de prospects grâce au site.

designManifest.iconDirection: A square emblem with a warm espresso-charcoal ground, a single bronze hand-trowel mark sweeping across a polished concrete sheen, fine terrazzo speckle in the corners — flat, confident, artisanal, no text.
designManifest.signatureMove: A circular foundry-style guarantee seal stamps the promise — oversized and slowly spinning over the hero photo, mounted static beside the guarantee band — backed by a fine terrazzo-aggregate speckle (bronze/indigo/cream dots) that frames every dark section, plus a persistent click-to-call bar so the phone is always one tap away.
designManifest.summary: An Italian-craftsman identity that treats every poured floor as a signed work — a warm espresso-and-limestone palette with a terrazzo-aggregate speckle and a foundry-style guarantee seal stamping the owner's personal promise across the site.
designManifest.typography: Fraunces (high-contrast warm display serif, Italian-artisanal voice) paired with Archivo (sturdy industrial grotesque body/UI)

promptHistory.changeNotes:
Initial build of a bilingual (FR primary / EN) lead-generation site for Le P'tit Italien, a Quebec concrete-floor finisher. Concept 'Terrazzo & Truelle': warm espresso/limestone palette with bronze metallic accents, a terrazzo-speckle texture, a spinning foundry-style guarantee seal carrying the owner's slogan, and an always-visible click-to-call bar. Includes home, réalisations gallery (with category filter + lightbox), services, témoignages, conseils blog, and contact form. Full in-PWA admin backend with dashboard and CRUD for projects, services, testimonials and posts, including image upload and AI image generation.

Admin enrichment: (1) Rebuilt the dashboard (admin.ejs) with a welcome banner, a highlighted demandes-reçues stat, and a richer 5-card module grid (Réalisations, Services, Témoignages, Conseils, Paramètres) with icons + live counts and obvious arrows. (2) Added a full admin Paramètres page (admin-settings.ejs) + route + sidebar link to manage FUNCTIONAL data: business name, contact phone/email/address and service area (which drive the tel: links, contact page and footer) plus logo/hero/about images with upload + live preview, all wired to the existing PUT /api/admin/settings and upload endpoints. (3) Enriched every CRUD module page (admin-shell) with a search/filter toolbar, a live item-count badge, an explicit Actions column header, hover rows and context-aware empty states — full create/edit/delete already intact and preserved. (4) Added accessible focus-visible outlines across admin + public buttons, inputs, nav and module cards; improved muted-text contrast in footer/testimonial roles. (5) Added og:type, og:image and twitter:card meta to the public header and associated <label for> ids on the contact form. Services remain the admin-managed functional offering set (name, price_note, featured, ordering). No routes/data flows removed; all {{IMG_*}} placeholder tokens preserved byte-for-byte.
